name: App Icon Orbit
summary: App icons or interface cards gather in a ring around a central brand mark or headline, then turn, glow or change state together. It shows the product as the hub that connects or replaces many tools.
when_to_use: Showing that the product connects to or replaces many other apps
Landing an outcome beat where scattered tools become one place
Turning a ring of broken or alerting tools into healthy ones

slots.name: hub
slots.what: the central brand mark, ring or headline the icons orbit

slots.name: icons
slots.what: a set of generic app icons, logo badges or small interface cards

slots.name: status_badge
slots.what: a small badge on each icon, such as an alert dot that becomes a check

slots.name: caption
slots.what: a short line beside or under the ring, built word by word with the narration

slots.name: background
slots.what: a gradient field that can shift colour to mark the change

steps: Start on the background, fading up from dark or out of the previous zoom
Bring in the hub at the centre
Fly or fan the icons into a ring around it, one after another
Change their state together: glow, swap to full colour, pop status badges, or shift the background
Rotate the ring slowly while the caption builds
Exit by drifting the ring out of frame, zooming through or flashing to white

build.gsap: One timeline per scene. Position icons on a circle with trigonometry inside a rotating container; stagger them in with scale and opacity from small, using a back out ease for a slight overshoot, or along curved paths from the corners with motion blur. Tween the background gradient and swap icon filters on one beat, pop the status badges with a short back out stagger, then run a slow linear rotation on the container and a power in drift for the exit.
build.remotion: One Sequence for the ring; each icon gets its own spring delayed by its index for the entrance, with position computed from its angle; the container's rotation is a linear interpolate over the scene; a nested Sequence drives the state change and badge springs; a final Sequence handles the drift or flash out.

sound: No typical sound. Music carries most of these scenes; a chime or click can mark icons arriving or a state change, but each comes from a single video.
caveats: Few videos, and several members are very short slivers split by the cut detector from one continuous move, so the measured length runs short.
No motion events or patterns were measured, so the build notes come from shot descriptions only.
Each sound cue comes from only one or two videos.
